name: EU Green Taxonomy Impact on European Banks - Capital Reallocation Analysis 2026-2028

slides.title: EU Green Taxonomy Impact on European Banks
slides.content:
Capital Reallocation Analysis 2026-2028

Lucia Moretti
European Banks Equity Research
Milan Investment Bank

European Banking Conference 2026
Frankfurt, March 11, 2026
slides.notes: Opening slide. Introduce topic and scope.

slides.title: Capital Reallocation Model - Core Assumptions
slides.content:
Key drivers of 15-20% portfolio shift:

1. Regulatory pressure: ECB supervisory expectations
2. Investor demand: ESG mandates from asset managers
3. Funding cost advantage: green bonds 20-30bps cheaper
4. Risk weight benefits: potential 15% RWA reduction for green assets

Model time horizon: 2026-2028
Covered banks: 11 EU SIFIs
slides.notes: THIS IS CRITICAL SLIDE. Walk through each driver slowly. Emphasize that this is conservative estimate - actual shift could be larger.

slides.title: Aggregate Capital Impact - EU Banking Sector
slides.content:
Total capital reallocation required: €180-240bn by 2028

Breakdown by country:
- Germany: €65bn (largest brown asset exposure)
- France: €55bn
- Italy: €35bn
- Spain: €25bn
- Nordic: €15bn (already advanced)

CET1 impact: -50 to -200bps depending on starting position
slides.notes: Clients will focus on CET1 impact. Be ready to explain why range is wide: depends on current green ratio and speed of transition.

slides.title: Bank-by-Bank Impact Analysis
slides.content:
Winners (already >30% green-aligned):
- Nordea: 42% green, minimal capital need
- DNB: 38% green
- SEB: 35% green

Mid-pack (20-30% green, manageable transition):
- BNP Paribas: 28% green
- Société Générale: 24% green
- Intesa Sanpaolo: 22% green

Laggards (<20% green, heavy capital requirement):
- Deutsche Bank: 18% green, €15bn need
- Commerzbank: 16% green
- UniCredit: 19% green
slides.notes: THIS SLIDE WILL GENERATE MOST QUESTIONS. Have bank-specific data ready. Clients will ask about their holdings.

slides.title: Implementation Timeline and Key Milestones
slides.content:
2026 Q2: ECB publishes supervisory expectations
2026 Q4: Banks must disclose green asset ratio in Pillar 3
2027 Q2: First annual green transition plans required
2027 Q4: Potential RWA benefits for green assets introduced
2028 Q2: Full taxonomy compliance mandatory

Regulatory certainty: HIGH
Implementation flexibility: MEDIUM
slides.notes: Timeline is locked in by EU regulation. Only implementation details are flexible. This gives banks 2-year runway but clock is ticking.

name: EU Green Taxonomy Impact on European Banks - Frankfurt Conference Version (Feb 2026)

slides.title: EU Green Taxonomy Impact on European Banks
slides.content:
Capital Reallocation Analysis 2026-2028

Lucia Moretti
European Banking Research Associate
Milan Investment Bank

European Banking Conference 2026
Frankfurt, February 26, 2026
slides.notes: Opening slide - 30 seconds. Introduce self, desk coverage (11 EU SIFI banks), research focus.

slides.title: Executive Summary
slides.content:
• EU Green Taxonomy introduces capital allocation pressure for banks with high carbon-intensive loan portfolios
• Italian banks (UniCredit, Intesa, BPM) face moderate transition costs vs German peers
• Estimated CET1 impact: 10-30bps by 2028 depending on portfolio mix
• Green asset ratio disclosure (EBA draft RTS Q3 2026) will increase transparency and investor scrutiny
• Strategic repositioning underway: UniCredit targeting 40% green asset ratio by 2028
slides.notes: Key takeaways - 2 minutes. Emphasize CET1 impact range and disclosure timeline.

slides.title: Methodology & Data Sources
slides.content:
• EBA Green Asset Ratio Disclosure Standards (Draft Feb 2026)
• ECB Banking Supervision Climate Risk Guidance
• Bank-level green asset disclosures (UniCredit, Intesa, BNP, Deutsche)
• Proprietary capital model incorporating Basel IV output floor
• Stress scenario: 50% reduction in carbon-intensive lending by 2028
slides.notes: Methodology overview - 2 minutes. Cite EBA draft RTS, ECB guidance. Mention Basel IV integration.
